finding: The shifted fraud profile did not evade the model. Recall was HIGHER in the shifted phase (100%) than in the PaySim-style phase (71%), with worse precision in both. Two reasons, both of which have to be fixed before this demo means anything: (1) Feast was not materialised in this session, so every sender lookup missed and every transaction was scored with default history features; (2) the model over-flags this synthetic traffic generally, so 'caught' is cheap. The performance flow, the label replay and the maturity join all ran correctly end-to-end on real infrastructure; it is the scenario that needs rework.
note: Phases split at the median decision time; each phase is 380 decisions.
